pairs.l: 1 — claims the most demanding part is in the post-production phase?
2 — says they created a film that came short of their professional expectations?
3 — states that a film will be successful if you know exactly what you want your film to achieve from the start?
4 — believes that not connecting with the audience can be detrimental to a film?
5 — says the success of a film depends on when you bring together and how you balance different aspects?
6 — admits they have enjoyed a limited period of success working in the film industry?
7 — argues that a filmmaker won't succeed if they don't have a strong artistic background?
8 — states they enjoyed the support of the experts they gathered for the project?
9 — says that the filmmaker's final product justifies the money they are making?
10 — finds that being well-organised initially can tip the scale of success in the later stages?
11 — mentions that, based on their experience, creating a film can be a strenuous process?
12 — suggests that you need to be passionate about your filmmaking project to succeed?

r1.exp: 1=B (Bert: 'Especially the period AFTER THE LAST SCENE HAS BEEN SHOT that involves EDITING, CGI, MARKETING etc'). 2=C (Connie: 'I found my work DIDN'T SUCCEED TO THE EXTENT I WAS HOPING'). 3=E (Emma: 'it's so important to make sure the director has a FULLY ROUNDED VISION of what their MESSAGE AS AN AUTHOR is going to be'). 4=B (Bert: 'the importance of how IT IS RECEIVED BY THE PUBLIC, which is KEY TO ITS SUCCESS OR DEMISE'). 5=C (Connie: 'filmmaking is not about any ONE THING, as it is about TIMING AND LOTS OF DIFFERENT FACTORS FALLING IN PLACE'). 6=A (Abigail: 'And that was that, AT LEAST FOR THE TIME BEING' = limited period). 7=D (David: 'the fate of the film will be decided by the filmmaker's... CREATIVE IMAGERY AND SOUND... by the AESTHETICS of it all'). 8=C (Connie: 'made with a GREAT TEAM who were ready to go that EXTRA MILE'). 9=D (David: 'a WELL-DESERVED ONE, even if the REWARDS ARE CONSIDERABLE'). 10=F (Francis: 'TAKE THE TIME FOR THIS and you can expect a more STREAMLINED PROCESS in post-production'). 11=A (Abigail: 'I couldn't have been MORE WRONG... how hard could that be? — IN RETROSPECT'). 12=F (Francis: 'PERSISTENT EXCITEMENT creates pressure, and pressure creates GOOD FILMS').

r13.exp: 'ENORMOUS, ELABORATE MOTIFS, often tens of metres across' = složeni uzorci = B.

r14.exp: 'The crops would ALWAYS SPRING BACK INTACT' = nije bilo fizičke štete biljkama = A.

r15.exp: 'The ideal opportunity for NEWSPAPER EDITORS. They seized on the regular opportunities for writing extensive articles' = novinari imali najviše koristi = C.

r16.exp: 'Arenas of CONFLICT during the miners' strike... VIOLENT CONFRONTATIONS between police... RAVE CULTURE' = mjesta čestih javnih nemira = D.

r17.exp: 'A FURTHER BLOSSOMING OF LAND-BASED ART' = proširenje repertoara umjetničkog izražaja = D.

r18.exp: 'It could never be MONETISED... their VERY SHORT-LIVED WORK' = nije trajno = A.

r19.exp: 'Stuck in repetitive, unhelpful thought patterns that make us feel OVERWHELMED. (19)____. Also, OTHER AREAS OF OUR LIVES can be affected, as well as our RELATIONSHIPS.' → D: This can NEGATIVELY IMPACT OUR MOOD and, ultimately, HOW WE WORK.

r20.exp: 'Overthinking leads to mind reading. (20)____. Our NEGATIVE commentary analyses behaviours and concludes someone's intention was negative.' → G: It results in us MAKING ASSUMPTIONS about what was MEANT BY THEIR COMMENT, or READING BETWEEN THE LINES of an email or text.

r21.exp: 'There are STRATEGIES that can help you stop overthinking. (21)____. You will FIRST NEED TO BE AWARE of your overthinking.' → A: Like any new POSITIVE BEHAVIOUR that you undertake, THEY TAKE TIME AND PRACTICE.

r22.exp: 'Focus on possible solutions – dwelling on the problem is NOT HELPFUL. (22)____. WRITE IT DOWN.' → H: INSTEAD OF ASKING WHY something happened, ASK IF THERE IS AN ANSWER TO THE PROBLEM.

r23.exp: 'Revisit this in 24 hours. (23)____. This is the actual process of finding PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS.' → E: IF IT IS STILL A CONCERN, then you can PROCEED TO PROBLEM SOLVING.

r24.exp: 'Healthy and strategic distraction can help us minimise overthinking. (24)____. There are SO MANY OTHER THINGS you can do to TAKE YOUR MIND OFF.' → C: EXERCISE, take part in a conversation about something else, WATCH A SHOW YOU LOVE, or work on another project.

r25.exp: 'Dogs NOT ONLY process the meaning of words BUT ALSO pick up on the emotional tone' — korelativna konstrukcija: not only... but also.

r26.exp: 'Dogs are ADEPT AT understanding non-verbal cues' — fiksna prijedložna kolokacija: adept at = vješt u.

r27.exp: 'The degree TO WHICH a dog can understand' — fiksna konstrukcija: the degree to which = mjera u kojoj.

r28.exp: 'As SEEN in studies on puppies' responses' — pasivna konstrukcija: as seen in = kako je vidljivo u (istraživanjima).

r29.exp: 'The topic REMAINS actively debated' — 'remain' + adjective/participle = ostaje (u određenom stanju).

r30.exp: 'Differs from ours, WITH each species having unique cognitive abilities' — 'with' + gerund za popratnu okolnost.

r31.exp: 'The remarkable bond SHARED between our two species' — 'shared' = dijeljeni, zajednički.

r32.exp: 'Development of assistive TECHNOLOGIES for people with disabilities' — fiksna kolokacija: assistive technologies = asistivne/pomažuće tehnologije.

r33.exp: 'Intuitive design, HOWEVER, is often used informally to describe designs that are easy to use' — 'however' za kontrast (experts can't agree on a definition, however it is often used informally).

r34.exp: 'A user is able to understand and use a design IMMEDIATELY, or rather, without consciously thinking' — 'immediately' = odmah (bez svjesnog razmišljanja).

r35.exp: 'While there is NO standard definition' — 'no' za negiranje imenice (nema standardne definicije).

r36.exp: 'Some research groups HAVE WORKED towards building a clearer understanding' — present perfect: have + past participle.

r37.exp: 'Members ARGUE that intuition is not a feature of design' — 'argue' = tvrditi, zauzeti stav (akademski glagol za iznošenje argumenta).

r38.exp: 'If we want to EVALUATE how intuitive a design is' — 'evaluate' = procijeniti, vrednovati.

r39.exp: 'Based on principles from some OTHER domains that are well known to them' — 'other' = neki drugi (domeni).

r40.exp: 'Consumers DEMAND that they have instant access to whatever they need' — 'demand' = zahtijevati (potrošači zahtijevaju trenutni pristup).

sol.rubric: Esej 200-250 riječi. ZA sve veći jaz: tehnologija, drugačije vrijednosti, komunikacijski stilovi, ekonomske nejednakosti. ZA nestajanje razlika: zajednički interesi, bolja komunikacija, globalizacija, stariji usvajaju tech. Vlastito mišljenje.

w1.exp: Esej — ručno se ocjenjuje. Diskusijski esej (discuss both views + opinion). Viša razina: akademski stil, 200–250 riječi.
